_readme: Sample payload the GoHighLevel (GHL) chatbot/workflow webhook action should POST
to the Zapier 'Catch Raw Hook' trigger. `sample_payload` is a realistic example;
`field_schema` documents types, requirements, and validation rules (JSON has no
comment syntax, so schema notes live in the `description`/`validation` keys
instead of being interspersed as comments).

template_request.description: A modern landing page for a boutique coffee roastery, warm earth tones, hero section with a signup form for a subscription box.

contact.name.validation: 1-200 characters. Used only for email personalization.

contact.email.validation: Must match a standard email regex, e.g. /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/. Reject the request (respond to the chatbot with an error message) if invalid before ever calling the webhook.

contact.phone.validation: E.164 format preferred. Not used by the automation today; reserved for SMS confirmations in a future iteration.

template_request.description.source_in_ghl: Captured via a GHL Conversational AI / chatbot question such as 'Describe the website you want (business type, style, key sections).'
template_request.description.validation: 10-2000 characters. Trim whitespace. Strip control characters. This is the only field that reaches the Claude prompt, so basic profanity/length filtering in GHL is recommended before sending.

template_request.css_framework.source_in_ghl: Optional multiple-choice chatbot question or a custom field with a dropdown.
template_request.css_framework.validation: Must be one of allowed_values if present; otherwise defaults to 'none' in Step 1 (Parse & Validate).

template_request.template_variant.source_in_ghl: Optional multiple-choice chatbot question, e.g. 'What kind of site is this?'
template_request.template_variant.validation: Must be one of allowed_values if present; otherwise defaults to 'general'.

github_credentials.owner.source_in_ghl: A custom field collected once during onboarding (not re-asked every conversation, if avoidable).

github_credentials.repo.source_in_ghl: Custom field, collected once during onboarding.
github_credentials.repo.validation: 1-100 chars, matches /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/. Strip a trailing '.git' if present.

github_credentials.branch.source_in_ghl: Custom field; most users can leave this at the default.

github_credentials.personal_access_token.source_in_ghl: SECURITY-SENSITIVE — see security_notes below before wiring this up.
github_credentials.personal_access_token.validation: Must match /^(ghp_|github_pat_)/. Never log this value in GHL workflow history or Zapier Zap History (mark the Zapier field as sensitive if your plan supports it).

meta.source.validation: Fixed value — lets the Zap distinguish this trigger source if the same webhook URL is ever reused for other automations.

meta.submitted_at.source_in_ghl: {{now}} or a GHL workflow 'Current Date/Time' variable.
meta.submitted_at.validation: Must parse as a valid date; used for logging and dedupe.

ghl_configuration_notes: 1. In GHL, build a Conversational AI / Chatbot flow (or a form) that asks the user for the website description, and optionally the CSS framework and template variant as quick-reply/dropdown questions.

2. Collect github_credentials.owner, .repo, and .personal_access_token via a one-time onboarding custom field set on the Contact record (Settings > Custom Fields), rather than asking for the token in every chat — this avoids re-transmitting a long-lived secret repeatedly and lets you rotate it in one place.
3. Add a 'Webhook' action as the final step of the GHL Workflow, method POST, URL = the Zapier 'Catch Raw Hook' URL from zapier_zap_config.json.

4. Set the webhook Content-Type to application/json and build the JSON body using GHL's merge-field syntax to match the sample_payload shape above exactly (field names and nesting matter — Step 1 of the Zap maps by exact key path).

5. Add a custom header, e.g. X-Webhook-Secret: <shared secret>, configured identically in both GHL and the Zap's Step 1 validator, so the Zap can reject spoofed requests that aren't actually from your GHL workflow.
6. Test using GHL's built-in 'Test Workflow' / webhook test action before going live, and confirm the payload lands correctly in Zapier's trigger test data.
security_notes: Sending a raw GitHub Personal Access Token through a chatbot conversation is inherently risky: GHL logs conversation and workflow history, and that history may include the token in plaintext.

Recommended mitigation for the MVP: collect the PAT once via a secure onboarding form (not the chatbot) and store it as a GHL custom field on the contact, scoped with the minimum required permissions (fine-grained PAT, single repo, Contents: Read & write, short expiration with a renewal reminder).

Recommended mitigation for Phase 2: replace raw PAT collection entirely with a GitHub App installation flow (OAuth), so users authorize access via GitHub's own consent screen and Zapier/your backend stores only a short-lived installation token — no PAT ever passes through GHL or chat.
